topic: What trade-offs exist between reflector aperture size and feed element redundancy in robust antenna design?
consensus_response: In robust antenna design, a key trade-off exists between reflector aperture size and feed element redundancy. Larger apertures improve gain but increase spillover loss, while redundant elements reduce pattern shape stability but provide improved robustness against failures. Mutual coupling between feed elements increases with redundancy, leading to decreased gain and increased complexity. The defocused reflector concept mitigates multipath effects by introducing center offset o, improving pattern shape stability in case of feed element failures. A hybrid design combining phased arrays and defocused reflectors can maintain system/network performance even in case of individual or multiple feed element failures.

The defocused reflector concept is also discussed as a method to mitigate multipath effects and improve robustness against feed failures.
